title: Monsters Loose — timed narrative v02
note: Broad editorial scene groupings, not a shot list. Anchors remain approximate. Original notes are not marked addressed. Lyric corrections remain pending in this pass.

cards.text:
An obscure creature detail foreshadows what is coming.
The swamp surrounds a secret monster zoo and laboratory.

Meet our keeper and singer: capable, alert, expecting trouble.
The creatures remain mostly hidden.

A breached enclosure hints that something has slipped out.
The keeper hears trouble before we see its source.

Illustrated creature faces hint at the hybrids made here.
The keeper plays with expressions; the real monsters stay hidden.

Her equipment hints at a special restraining lasso.
A garbled PA announcement warns that something is wrong.

Explore the zoo's different habitats and small enclosures.
Building cage-rattles suggest something much larger inside.

Meet the laboratory team and its reckless scientist.
A town left burning recalls what their last creation could do.

The scientist proposes something even bigger and meaner.
The keeper looks upward: its full scale stays out of view.

Return to the zoo as the threat of escape builds.
OPEN: use this breathing space to establish what comes next.

The keeper welcomes visitors to this strangely cheerful zoo.
Her account begins to reveal how dangerous its residents are.

Now demonstrate her lasso skills: she keeps the monsters in.
She enjoys giving the visitors a playful scare.

A skeptical child sees through the keeper's teasing.
Real danger nearby makes that confidence funny and uneasy.

Reveal the variety: jungle, desert, lake, ice and alien habitats.
Save the creatures of the surrounding swamp for later.

Imagine the monsters in the wild, where they were captured.
Their version of hide-and-seek is really hunting.

A countdown gathers monsters into a showdown.
Visitors root for favorites; the contest soon narrows to two.

Two final rivals face off while spectators back their choices.
OPEN: a natural clash or something staged at the zoo?

An impossible monster-movie kick sends a rival over mountains.
Battered but resilient, it prepares to return to the fight.

The scientists regroup to imagine their next creation.
Perhaps the visitors join this dangerously enthusiastic discussion.

Reveal the scientist's plan: unlock the zoo and let them loose.
This circles back to the warnings we heard at the beginning.

A huge creature shrinks small enough to escape.
Abilities once contained now become ways out.

A small, insect-like creature grows to enormous size.
Its enclosure cannot hold it.

Another creature becomes smoke and slips through a keyhole.
An apparently impenetrable door is no defense.

The child refuses to believe it; the keeper insists it is true.
Is she exaggerating, or should you always trust the tour guide?

Widen the story to the escape unfolding around them.
Some people seem to enjoy it as a show rather than a disaster.

Return to the faces introduced on the illustrated zoo sign.
Now the audience meets the actual creatures.

Return to the swamp outside the zoo: creatures live here too.
POSSIBILITY: they and the scientist share a secret escape plan.

Revisit our favorite monsters as they finally break free.
Even the keeper's lasso skills cannot hold them all.

Collected and created monsters are free to be themselves.
The ending relaxes into natural behavior, rather than a rampage.
